question.problem:
Let $X$ be a random variable with the probability density function shown below. What is the mode of $X?$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9}{x}^{2},\, & 0\le x\le 3 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The mode of a random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ is the value of $x$ at the global maximum of $f(x).$

To find the global maximum of $f(x),$ we find the critical points of $f(x)$ and then apply the candidates test.

First, we find the critical points.

- The piece of $f(x)$ defined on $0\le x\le 3$ is $f(x)=\frac{1}{9}{x}^{2}.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{2}{9}x,\end{aligned}
$$

and solving ${f}^{′}(x)=0,$ we get

$$
\frac{2}{9}x=0\,⟹\,x=0.
$$

The point $x=0$ is in the interval $[0,3],$ so we keep it.

- The derivative doesn't exist at the endpoints $x=0,3.$ So, these are critical points as well.

Now, we evaluate $f(x)$ at the critical points $x=0,3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot {0}^{2}=0 \\ f(3) & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot {3}^{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compare all of the values above. The largest value is

$$
f(3)=1
$$

Therefore, the mode of $X$ is $3.$
